channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Anthropic's Solution to AI Danger Is 'Quite Vague': Opinion
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Parmy Olson discusses Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei's proposal that AI labs should slow down their most cutting-edge research. "Pacing or slowing down does also just essentially kick the can down the road," Olson says on Bloomberg Television. "Dario's essay was quite vague in terms of how he thinks that should happen." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: M&G's Municchi Says Investors 'More Wary' About AI Trade
item.description: Maria Municchi, multi asset fund manager at M&G Investments, discusses the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade after leaders of the biggest firms proposed slowing the technology’s development. She tells Bloomberg Television that while "price will continue to behave pretty well," markets are becoming "a little bit more wary" about whether the capex boom will translate into delivered earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI President on Doing Business in the Wake of Hugging Face
item.description: According to OpenAI President Greg Brockman, the models that escaped their sandbox and hacked into Hugging Face's servers had yet to go through alignment training. That they were able to break free of the testing environment was not a surprise to OpenAI, but what has happened since has forced them to rethink some things. Today, we talk to Brockman about what OpenAI has learned since the hacking incident and we discuss why he thinks the conversation around model development has to change. We also talk about how OpenAI collaborates and communicates with competitors like Anthropic, how he thinks models should be evaluating what counts as “good writing,” and, of course, we get his thoughts on how seriously we should be worried about the AI doomsday scenarios. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Rebuffs AI Warnings as Rivalry Clouds US Safety Talks
item.description: China criticized dire warnings about AI’s risks after leading US technology executives backed calls to slow the development of advanced models and warned that a Chinese advantage could threaten American national security.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: ICBC, HSBC Among Major Lenders on $30 Billion ByteDance Loan
item.description: ByteDance Ltd., the developer of TikTok, has signed a $29.6 billion loan with more than two dozens lenders, including Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Ltd. and HSBC Holdings Plc, in one of Asia’s biggest dollar-denominated deals this year.
item.dc:creator: Aileen Chuang

item.title: Data Center Firm Firmus Said to Seek $5 Billion in Australia IPO
item.description: Firmus Technologies Pty is looking to raise as much as $5 billion in an initial public offering in Australia, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Julia Fioretti

item.title: OpenAI’s Altman Voices Support for ‘Pacing’ AI Development
item.description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman on Sunday added his support to the idea of “pacing” AI development, so that cutting-edge models don’t outrun the ability of humans to maintain control.
item.dc:creator: Debby Wu

item.title: Ligent Technologies Seeks $727 Million in Hong Kong IPO
item.description: AI computing networks maker Ligent Technologies Inc. is seeking to raise as much as HK$5.7 billion ($727 million) in a Hong Kong initial public offering, adding to a surge of listings this year tied to the global artificial intelligence buildout.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: Ed Conway on the Fragile World of Global Trade
item.description: Merryn Somerset Webb talks with Ed Conway, economics and data editor at Sky News and author of "Trade World," about the vast and often invisible supply chains behind the things we buy and whether decades of globalization have made economies more resilient or dangerously dependent. They also discuss China’s manufacturing advantage, and whether the UK and Europe can rebuild their industrial base without giving up the cheap goods consumers have come to expect. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Bans Drone Ownership in Beijing After Citic Tower Crash
item.description: Beijing has banned the possession and use of recreational drones as part of moves to bolster security in the capital after a light plane crashed into the city’s tallest skyscraper in June.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Chinese Local Banks Urged to Boost Clients’ Yuan Hedging
item.description: Some local branches of China’s foreign exchange regulator are urging banks to encourage their clients to hedge more of their currency exposure, signaling an intensifying campaign to shield companies from related risk.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: China Spy Chief Warns of AI Risks as Anthropic CEO Urges Brakes
item.description: China’s top intelligence official delivered one of Beijing’s most detailed warnings yet about AI, saying rapid advances in the technology could threaten political stability and critical infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Chevron Australia President on LNG outlook
item.description: Balaji Krishnamurthy, President of Chevron in Australia, discusses the outlook for LNG supply and demand, and pricing levels, as energy disruptions continue on Middle East tensions. He speaks with Haslinda Amin, on the sidelines of Gastech in Bangkok, on "Bloomberg: The Asia Trade". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Z.AI’s Cash Burn Drives Alibaba-Like HK Fundraising Spree
item.description: Z.AI Co. dashed back to Hong Kong’s equity market as soon as its last lockup expired, underscoring a cash burn rate that leaves the artificial intelligence model maker’s hunger to take advantage of any fundraising opportunity.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: Samsung, SK Hynix Reject Kepco’s Power Grid Prepayment Plan
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. have rejected a proposal from Korea Electric Power Corp. that would have seen the two pay in advance for electricity in order to finance the construction of grids to power new technology clusters.
item.dc:creator: Hyunbin Kim

item.title: AI Bosses Risk Clash With Wall Street and Trump Over Safety
item.description: Anthropic PBC and OpenAI will have to weigh their calls to tap the brakes on artificial intelligence development against forces in the tech industry, financial markets and the Trump administration that are likely to resist any substantial slowdown.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Frier and Michael Shepard

item.title: SoftBank Gets Upsized $11.9 Billion Loan in OpenAI Funding Push
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. secured an $11.87 billion loan to support its investment in US artificial intelligence firm OpenAI, people familiar with the matter said, up from its earlier target of $10 billion.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang

item.title: Amazon Halts Operations With 21 Air After Fatal Miami Crash
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. suspended work with cargo carrier 21 Air LLC, which operated the Sept. 6 flight that overran the runway at Miami and killed five people on the ground.
item.dc:creator: Angus Whitley

item.title: OCBC's Vasu on the Stock Retreat After AI Warning Calls
item.description: Asian stocks and US equity-index futures retreated after major artificial intelligence companies called for a slowdown in the technology’s development. OCBC Investment Strategy MD Vasu Menon has more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Asia Chip Stocks Drop as AI Chiefs Urge Slower Model Development
item.description: Asian semiconductor and equipment stocks fell Monday as higher oil prices and calls from major AI leaders to slow model development weighed on sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Winnie Hsu, Youkyung Lee and Matthew Burgess
